name: Lake Bled
title: Holidays in Lake Bled
intro: A church on an island, a castle on a cliff and a lakeside Christmas market under the Julian Alps. Here's what Lake Bled is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Late November to early January brings the Winter Fairytale market and lights round the lake, with snow on the mountains. May, June and September are warm and good for swimming and walks. July and August are lovely but busy.

things.name: Bled Winter Fairytale
things.blurb: A Christmas market on the lakeshore with wooden huts, lights, a skating area and mulled wine.

things.name: Pletna boat to the island
things.blurb: A wooden rowing boat takes you to the island church, where you can ring the wishing bell.

things.name: Bled Castle
things.blurb: A cliff-top castle with a little museum, a printing workshop and the best view of the lake.

things.name: Bled cream cake
things.blurb: Try a slice of kremšnita, the local custard and cream cake, at a lakeside café.

things.name: Straža hill
things.blurb: A small slope above the lake with sledging and easy skiing in winter and a summer toboggan run.

things.name: Ljubljana
things.blurb: Slovenia's small, friendly capital has its own big Christmas market, about 40 minutes away.

faqs.question: Is Lake Bled good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's small, safe and easy to walk round, and the boat ride and castle are big hits with children.

faqs.question: When is the Christmas market on?
faqs.answer: Usually from late November until early January. It's smaller and calmer than the big city markets.

faqs.question: Is there snow at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Often on the mountains, sometimes by the lake. Ski areas like Vogel and Kranjska Gora are under an hour away.

faqs.question: Can we walk round the lake?
faqs.answer: Yes, the path is about 6 km and flat, so it's fine for buggies. Allow around two hours.
